title: From the cracks of the earth (Kern ch. 14)
word: From the cracks of the earth
hook: countless bodhisattvas rise from the ground, pupils of the Buddha from long ago
tomorrow: The lifespan of the Tathagata (Kern ch. 15)

segments.voice: Yesterday, four ways to teach calmly, and a king who kept one jewel in his hair for the deed beyond all others. Your line: the jewel in the topknot. What did you explain slowly? Day one thousand one hundred sixty-nine.

In spring, a crack in the sidewalk fills with green. Nobody planted it. Nobody watered it. It was down there the whole time, working in the dark, and one day it's just up. Chapter fourteen of the Lotus Sutra opens with an offer of help. Bodhisattvas who've come from other worlds stand up and say to the Buddha: let us protect this sutra here, after you're gone. A generous offer. A sensible one. And the Buddha turns it down. No need, he says. This world already has its own. Then the ground starts to split. Today: from the cracks of the earth.
screen: `GREEN IN A SIDEWALK CRACK.` → `AN OFFER OF HELP.` → `NO NEED.`

segments.voice: First, the offer, and the refusal. The visiting bodhisattvas mean well. But the Buddha says this world has bodhisattvas of its own who will keep the sutra after him. Second, the earth opens. All across this world the ground cracks, and up from the space beneath it rise bodhisattvas beyond counting, bodies shining gold, each with a great company of followers. They go up to the jeweled stupa still hanging in the sky, and bow to the two Buddhas seated there. Four lead them, and all four of their names speak of conduct: superior, boundless, pure, and firm. Third, nobody knows them. Maitreya, who is said to be the next Buddha, has never seen a single one of them, and neither has anyone else in the assembly. So he asks: who are these? The Buddha's answer: I taught them. All of them. Here, in this world, since my awakening. They've been living below, studying quietly, staying away from crowds. Fourth, the puzzle. Maitreya is honest about how strange that sounds. You awakened not so long ago, he says. How could you have taught so many? It's like a young man with dark hair pointing at a crowd of white-haired elders and saying, these are my sons, while they nod and say, he's our father. Who would believe it? The chapter ends with that question in the air, and tomorrow's chapter answers it. This is the week's last day. Lay its chapters side by side: the attendant and the son, the one who teaches a single verse, a girl from under the sea, two women waiting to be named, and now a crowd nobody knew was there. All week, the Lotus kept counting the people nobody was counting.
screen: `VISITORS OFFER TO HELP.` · `NO NEED: THE EARTH OPENS.` · `I TAUGHT THEM ALL.` · `A YOUNG MAN WITH OLD SONS.` · then, large: `THEY ROSE FROM THE EARTH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: notice something that grew quietly. Settle, and feel the ground under you holding you up. Let the breath come and go. Now bring to mind one thing in your life that grew while nobody was watching. A friendship that deepened without a big moment. A child who's suddenly taller. A patience you didn't have a few years ago. A plant on a windowsill. Just notice it, and how long it was working underground before it showed. Rest with it, and with the breath. The bell holds the time.
From the cracks of the earth. Bodhisattvas beyond counting, taught by the Buddha in this world, rise from beneath it when he says no outside help is needed. Today's word.
screen: `FROM THE CRACKS OF THE EARTH — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: they rose from the earth. Today, tell one person about something in them that grew quietly. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-nine.

howItsDone: In Mahayana communities that read the Lotus Sutra, the bodhisattvas who rise from the earth are honored as the ones entrusted with the sutra in this world, and some schools, including Nichiren Buddhism, give them and their leader a central place.

fork.setup: you're Maitreya. the Buddha says he taught every one of these countless bodhisattvas. what do you say?
options: how? it's like a young man calling old men his sons.
nothing: you don't question the Buddha.
fork.reveal: Maitreya says it plainly: a young man with dark hair, white-haired elders calling him father. who'd believe it? tomorrow's chapter answers.

original.note: Sanskrit: a being set on awakening, like the ones who rise from the earth in chapter fourteen.

trapdoor: what you thought: an army of saints appears out of nowhere.
what it means: bodhisattvas the Buddha taught in this world, living quietly below it, rise when he says no outside help is needed.
what a scholar hears: Maitreya's puzzle, a young father with aged sons, sets up the next chapter's answer about how long the Buddha has really lived.

notes: Chapter paraphrased from Kern (1884) ch. 14, not quoted (wording unverified). Text numbers (bodhisattvas 'equal to the sands of Ganges', the age of the young man and the old men, the length of their praise) deliberately left out under the claims rule.
The four leaders (Visistacaritra, Anantacaritra, Visuddhacaritra, Supratisthitacaritra) are given only as 'names that speak of conduct: superior, boundless, pure, firm'; confirm the glosses.
'Maitreya, who is said to be the next Buddha' is attributed; confirm.
howItsDone: Nichiren Buddhism's emphasis on the bodhisattvas of the earth and Visistacaritra (Jogyo); confirm the general phrasing.
